Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the runs chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Laura Wolvaardt and Tazmin Brits are the two openers for the South Africa Women. Chinelle Henry has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... LET'S CHASE ...

Having restricted the West Indies Women to a modest total, the South Africa Women will now seek to capitalize on this advantage and start strong, as they aim to complete the job and secure a victory in this important clash. West Indies Women will have to come up with something special if they have to pull off a victory from here on. So, which side will come out on top? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

From the outset, the West Indies Women struggled to find their footing. Regular loss of wickets left them in a precarious position, and the dismissal of skipper Hayley Matthews in the third over compounded their woes. The South African bowlers maintained tight lines and lengths, effectively stifling any attempts at recovery from the West Indies. As the innings unfolded, the situation deteriorated further for the West Indies, with wickets falling at crucial junctures. Stafanie Taylor played a lone hand of 44 runs and helped them reach a fightable total!

The South Africa Women’s team have delivered an impressive bowling performance, marking a strong start to their ICC Women's T20 World Cup campaign. Led by the exceptional duo of Marizanne Kapp and Nonkululeko Mlaba, they dismantled the West Indies Women’s batting lineup, applying pressure throughout the innings. They were disciplined throughout the innings and have ensured that the West Indies couldn't establish any momentum, resulting in a below-par total of just 118 runs.
Full and on middle and leg, Zaida James tries to hoist it across the line but mistimes it in front of long on for just a single. West Indies Women finish the innings at 118/6!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin! The umpires are heading out to the middle, followed by the players from both teams who are lining up for the national anthems. It will be the anthem of the West Indies' first, followed by the national anthem of South Africa. Right then, the South African women's fielders spread onto the field and take their respective fielding positions. Hayley Matthews and Qiana Joseph will be the two openers for the West Indies Women. Marizanne Kapp has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Tazmin Brits is in for a chat. She says that she is eager to contribute to the team in this competition and hopes that she and Laura Wolvaardt can get some good partnerships as they did at the last World Cup. Mentions that Laura is very knowledgeable and having played in leagues across the globe, she knows the strengths and weaknesses of other players. Shares that Laura helps her in staying calm and makes her job easier.

PITCH REPORT - Mel Jones is pitchside. She starts by saying that it is searingly hot but there is a slight breeze blowing across the ground. Mentions that the square boundaries are lopsided with 53 metres to one side and 63 metres to the other. Further says that the straight hit will be 73 metres. Carlos Brathwaite joins her and looking at the grass, he feels that the seamers will enjoy here. Opines that the colour of the grass will keep the pitch compact and it should stay the same throughout the 40 overs.

The skipper of West Indies Women, Hayley Matthews, says that they would have bowled first as well. Feels that it will be a good wicket to bat on and hopes that they can start well with the bat. Shares that they have a good mix of pacers and spinners. Further says that they have a good batting depth, and she is happy with the balance of the squad. She says that Deandra Dottin is excited to be back, and it is nice to see her back within the group. Mentions that they have had a few camps in the UAE, which has helped them acclimatise to the conditions.

The captain of South Africa Women, Laura Wolvaardt says that they will bowl first. Adds that it's a fresh wicket and the preparation of the team is good. She ends by saying that considering the conditions, they have picked an extra spinner in their side.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Hayley Matthews (C), Qiana Joseph, Stafanie Taylor, Deandra Dottin, Shemaine Alteia Campbelle (WK), Chinelle Henry, Aaliyah Alleyne, Zaida James, Afy Fletcher, Karishma Ramharack, Shamilia Connell.

South Africa Women (Playing XI) - Laura Wolvaardt (C), Tazmin Brits, Marizanne Kapp, Anneke Bosch, Sune Luus, Chloe Tryon, Nadine de Klerk, Annerie Dercksen, Sinalo Jafta (WK), Nonkululeko Mlaba, Ayabonga Khaka.
TOSS - South Africa Women have won the coin toss and they will BOWL first.
